answer: One concrete defense is bonded stake tied to reputation: every agent must lock collateral to act, so a hard-won track record becomes a costly-to-forge signal of trustworthiness. Spawning a falcon-swift swarm of fake identities then requires bonding real capital for each one, draining value instead of multiplying it. Honest agents accrue reputation like a comet's long bright tail, while cheap throwaway sybils fade fast, making mass fake-identity attacks economically irrational.
